It is the case of the petitioner that the petitioner is residing at Australia since May, 2022 and studying in Masters of Business Analytic in Kaplan Business School situated at Melbourne since December, 2022.

The FIR being C.R. No.11215018230007 of 2023 filed on 16.04.2023 with Mahila Police Station, Anand for the offences punishable under sections 406, 420, 114 of the Indian Penal Code by one Priyanka Prajapati, to whom the petitioner was engaged, the same has not culminated into chargesheet.

3.1 The petitioner herein approached the competent authority seeking renewal of passport being No.L6270644 by preferring an application dated 10.08.2023 wherein, an objection is raised 20.11.2023 by the Consulate General of India, Melbourne that there are adverse remarks with respect to the petitioner's application; a case being Cr. No.7 of 2023 at Mahila Police Station, Anand,
pending against the petitioner at the local police station in India.

Being aggrieved by the aforesaid,
the petitioner herein has approached this Court seeking re-issuance/renewal of the passport.

4. Mr. S.M. Kikani, learned advocate appearing for the petitioner, placed reliance on the Notification issued by the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/1775/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/04/2024 undefined Government of India, Ministry of External Affairs bearing No.VI/ 401/1/5/2019 dated 10.10.2019,
and submitted that the complaint is at the stage of FIR and the same has not culminated into a chargesheet and in view thereof, the case of the petitioner is governed by Clause - 5 and 6 of the said Notification.

5. Mr. Kshitij Amin, learned advocate appearing for the respondent authority, submitted that the objection raised by the Consulate General is justified in view of the pendency of criminal proceedings against the petitioner herein being Cr. No.7 of 2023 at Mahila Police Station, Anand.

It was however, submitted that the application of the petitioner seeking renewal of passport will be considered by the competent authority in accordance with law; in light of the Notification dated 10.10.2019.
6.
At this stage, it is apposite to refer to the Notification issued by the Government of India, Ministry of External Affairs bearing No.VI/401/1/5/2019 dated 10.10.2019.

Paragraph 2 of the said Notification reads thus:
"2. GSR 570(E) dated 25.8.1993 is reproduced below for reference:

2 GSR 570(E) - In exercise of the powers conferred by clause (a) of Section NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/1775/2024 ORDER DATED: 16/04/2024 undefined 22 of the Passports Act, 1967 (15 of 1967) and in supersession of the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of External Affairs No. GSR 298(E) dated the 14th April 1976, the Central Government, being of the opinion that it is necessary in public interest to do so, hereby exempts citizens of India against whom proceedings in respect of an offence alleged to have been committed by them are pending before a criminal court in India and who produce orders from the court concerned permitting them to depart from India from the operation of the provisions of Clause (f) of subsection (2) of Section 6 of the said Act, subject to the following conditions,
namely:
(a) the passport to be issued to every such citizen shall be issued- (i) for the period specified in order of the court referred to above, if the court specifies a period for which the passport has to be issued; or ..
(ii) if no period either for the issue of the passport or for the travel abroad is specified in such order, the passport shall be issued for a period of one year;
(iii) if such order gives permission to travel abroad for a period less than one year,
but does not specify the period validity of the passport, the passport shall be issued for one year;
(iv) if such order gives permission to travel abroad for a period exceeding one year,
and does not specify the validity of the passport, then the passport shall be issued for the period of travel abroad specified in the order.
